verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Apr 10, 2026', 'Orion spacecraft successfully returned'; R2: 'splashdown in the Pacific on Friday'; R3: 'Splashdown ... off the coast of San Diego'; R4: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean ... Apr 10, 2026'; R5: 'Artemis II splashes down in Pacific Ocean'; R6: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean'; R8: 'splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm successful splashdown in Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission marked a safe return for the crew after their trip around the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'successfully returned from its mission to circle the moon'; R2: 'returned from the moon ... triumphant homecoming ... crew extracted'; R3: 'welcome the Artemis II crew home'; R4: 'astronauts are back on Earth ... hale and hearty'; R6: 'returned to Earth after a 10-day mission to the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe safe, successful crew return after lunar flyby/mission around the moon.

verifications.claim: Footage of the reentry, parachute deployment, and splashdown is available from NASA, PBS, and major news outlets like WBAL-TV.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2 (PBS): 'Watch in our video player above' with reentry details; R3 (NASA): 'Watch live return coverage ... NASA’s YouTube channel'; R4 (WBAL-TV): 'FULL VIDEO: Watch Artemis II crew splashdown ... From parachute deployment to splashdown'; R6 (BBC): 'Watch the Artemis II re-entry: Separation, blackout, then splashdown'
verifications.reasoning: Specific sources (PBS R2, WBAL-TV R4, NASA R3/R8) provide video footage explicitly covering reentry, parachutes, and splashdown.

verifications.claim: NASA YouTube Channel features the complete live coverage, including atmospheric entry, heat shield performance, and capsule splashdown.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Watch live return coverage on NASA+ ... NASA’s YouTube channel'; timeline: '7:53 p.m.: ... first contact with the upper atmosphere', 'exposing its heat shield', '8:07 p.m.: ... splash down'; R8: 'NASA's YouTube channel ... continuous coverage ... entry interface ... heat shield ... splashdown'
verifications.reasoning: NASA sources confirm YouTube live coverage of entry, heat shield exposure/entry, and splashdown events.

verifications.claim: NBC News provides clips of the parachute deployment and splashdown in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R5: 'Artemis II splashes down in Pacific Ocean ... videos: "Artemis astronauts splash down on Earth", "Astronauts safely removed from Orion capsule", "Service module separates"'
verifications.reasoning: NBC (R5) has splashdown clips and related recovery videos, but parachute deployment not explicitly listed, though implied in splashdown sequence.

verifications.claim: BBC News covers the separation, blackout period, and final splashdown.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'Watch the Artemis II re-entry: Separation, blackout, then splashdown'
verifications.reasoning: BBC video title and description exactly match separation, blackout, and splashdown coverage.

verifications.claim: PBS Newshour offers video coverage of the crew returning to Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2 (PBS Newshour): 'Watch in our video player above. ... Artemis II crew splashes down on Earth after historic trip'
verifications.reasoning: PBS Newshour directly provides video of crew splashdown/return to Earth.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule splashed down west of San Diego around 8:07 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'off the San Diego coast'; R3: '8:07 p.m. EDT ... off the coast of San Diego'; R8: '5:07 p.m. PT (8:07 p.m. ET) ... off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm splashdown off San Diego coast (west) at exactly 8:07 p.m. EDT/ET.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule splashdown concluded a 10-day mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'nearly 10-day flight'; R3: 'Flight Day 10'; R4: 'nearly 10-day journey'; R5: '10-day mission'; R6: '10-day mission'; R8: '10 days circling'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources state splashdown concluded ~10-day mission.

verifications.claim: Recovery teams immediately began securing the capsule and retrieving the crew.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R2: 'recovery ship ... awaited the crew's arrival ... extract the crew'; R3: 'recovery team will be standing by ... extract the crew ... Within two hours after splashdown'
verifications.reasoning: Teams were ready post-splashdown to secure/retrieve crew, but 'immediately' is broader than 'within two hours'; supports prompt action.

verifications.claim: The securing of the capsule and retrieving of the crew was captured in live video feeds.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R2: 'screengrab from a livestream video ... crew module separates ... crew members ... after being extracted ... screengrab from a livestream'; R5: 'videos: "Astronauts hoisted by helicopter from splashdown site", "Astronauts safely removed from Orion capsule"'
verifications.reasoning: Livestreams captured separation/extraction moments, implying recovery, but not explicitly 'securing capsule and retrieving crew' in detail.
